publications.title: Robust Meta-Graph Learning: Exploring Multilevel Feature Interrelationships To Enhance Multimodal Time Series Prediction
publications.abstract:
The booming digital economy has provided unprecedented opportunities for enhancing prediction performance with multimodal time series data in a broad range of business analytics scenarios. In this study, we explore multilevel, asynchronous feature interrelationships in multimodal time series data and disentangle the intricate interrelationships with a design artifact named RMGL (for robust meta-graph learning). The design of RMGL is rooted in graph convolutional networks. The core of RMGL is a meta-graph composed of three hierarchically interconnected graphs, representing feature-, modality-, and timestep-wise interrelationships, respectively. The interconnections across the graphs allow feature representations to propagate simultaneously through a graph attention mechanism, thereby quantifying multilevel feature interrelationships with graph structures synchronously and efficiently. Furthermore, capitalizing on the low-pass nature of graph convolutional filters, RMGL introduces a weight regularization scheme to effectively learn the meta-graph for prediction. RMGL outperformed state-of-the-art alternatives in our empirical evaluation involving both regression (financial risk prediction) and classification (sentiment analysis, humor detection, and intent recognition) tasks. Ablation experiments, exploratory analyses, and economic value analysis indicate the utility of every design component in RMGL.
                  History: Accepted by Ram Ramesh, Area Editor for Data Science and Machine Learning.
                  Funding: G. Chen was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72522010, 72394371, 72301239, and 72550002]. S. Xiao was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72671226, 72301194, 72472058, and 72495133].
                  Supplemental Material: The software that supports the findings of this study is available within the paper and its Supplemental Information ( https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/suppl/10.1287/ijoc.2024.0933 ) as well as from the IJOC GitHub software repository ( https://github.com/INFORMSJoC/2024.0933 ). The complete IJOC Software and Data Repository is available at https://informsjoc.github.io/ .

publications.title: Multi-Timescale Transmission-Distribution Coordination Under Decision-Dependent Uncertainty for Enhancing Economic Performance and Operational Reliability
publications.abstract: Coordinated operation between the transmission network (TN) and distribution networks (DNs) is essential to accommodate the high penetration of distributed photovoltaic (PV). Two gaps remain in TN-DN coordination regarding multi-timescale scheduling and decision-dependent uncertainty (DDU) management. This paper proposes a multi-timescale TN-DN coordinated operation framework, which together provides DDU-aware uncertainty modeling and algorithm design. First, the framework architecture is presented, which includes a day-ahead stage at an hourly resolution and an intra-day stage at a 15-minute resolution. Then, the optimal day-ahead TN-DN coordinated scheduling strategy is developed, which includes day-ahead operation and hourly TN-DN power exchanges. Herein, an improved consensus alternating direction method of multipliers (C-ADMM) is proposed to accelerate the convergence of the multi-timescale TN-DN coordinated operation framework. Finally, the intra-day TN-DN scheduling model is formulated, in which a chance-constrained optimization is adopted to capture DDU characteristics for DNs. The chance constraints are further reformulated as robust constraints via a robust approximation approach to guarantee solution tractability. Case studies verify that the proposed framework increases the accommodation of distributed PV while enhancing the economic performance and operational reliability of ITDS.

publications.title: Conditional Distributionally Robust Optimization for Look-Ahead Power Dispatch With Heterogeneous Uncertainties
publications.abstract: This paper presents a look-ahead environmental-economic power dispatch model incorporating heterogeneous uncertainties. A novel distributionally robust dispersion control is integrated in the model for managing air pollutant emissions. This control approach captures the spatial and temporal distribution of emissions, aiming to minimize their contribution to air pollutant concentrations. Furthermore, the dispersion condition uncertainty is modeled on a finite support to enhance control robustness. As a result, the traditional infinite-support renewable energy uncertainty is combined with the proposed finite-support dispersion condition uncertainty in a distributionally robust optimization framework. A joint ambiguity set is thus formulated for the two heterogeneous and correlative uncertainties, which addresses the heterogeneity through conditional probability theory and captures the correlation by conditional expectation constraints. To solve the distributionally robust dispatch model, it is first converted into a tractable form that incorporates robust cost constraints, utilizing dual theory of infinite dimensional linear programming. A conditional column and constraint generation method is then developed to tackle the reformulated problem. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed dispersion control in improving air quality, and the computational efficiency of our solution methods.

publications.title: When does skewness matter in robust inventory management?
publications.abstract: We investigate the impact of skewed demand on robust inventory management. Including skewness in calculations leads to cubic constraints that prevent a standard two-stage method from deriving an explicit and tractable objective function. To overcome this roadblock, we propose a joint optimization method to directly derive the robust solution in a closed form. The joint optimization method is widely applicable to various robust inventory models with different ambiguity sets. The notable advantage is that we can obtain the final solution without deriving the objective function, so many tedious intermediate steps are circumvented. We conduct numerical experiments on industry data to demonstrate that our moment-based policies deliver more consistent performance than divergence-based policies. After obtaining various closed-form solutions, we demonstrate that including skewness in the model improves the profit generated by the robust optimal order quantity if either demand is bounded or the cost-to-price ratio is low, even though the sample moments used may not equal the population moments. Furthermore, under these conditions in which skewness should be included in the calculations, the firm’s expected profit, under the most unfavorable distribution, increases with variance but decreases with skewness. This result stands in contrast to findings in the economics and finance literature, where distributional ambiguity is not considered.

publications.title: Joint Assortment Planning and Inventory Control under General Choice Models
publications.abstract: We propose a constant-factor approximation framework for the joint assortment planning and inventory management problem, where customers substitute to less preferred in-stock products if more preferred products are out of stock. The customer arrivals follow an increasing-failure-rate (IFR) distribution, and customer purchasing behavior is governed by a discrete choice model with dynamic inventory availability. Our decision involves determining the initial inventory vector, subject to a capacity constraint. Our algorithm begins with a novel fluid relaxation that identifies at most two candidate assortments with the highest potential profitability. For each assortment, we construct a static-allocation-based lower bound on the expected total revenue for an inventory vector that stocks only the products in the assortment. The final inventory decision is the vector that maximizes the stronger of these two lower bounds. We establish a (κ/4−ε)-approximation guarantee for a broad class of substitutable choice models, in which adding products weakly decreases the choice probabilities of existing items, and for which the cardinality-constrained assortment optimization problem admits a κ-approximation algorithm. Our result provides the first constant-factor approximation ratios for this problem under several important choice models, including the Markov chain choice model and the mixture of MNL models. Moreover, our framework also achieves the state-of-the-art approximation ratio of 0.25 for the MNL choice model. Our guarantees can be further strengthened when the capacity constraint is relatively loose or when the demand distribution is deterministic or Poisson.

publications.title: SharkLang Governed AI v2.4.2 Security Review Release
publications.abstract: SharkLang Governed AI v2.4.2 is a security-review release dated 1 November 2026. This Zenodo record is deposited on 1 November 2026. It provides the final review archive for inspection and reproducible evaluation. The archive includes the SharkLang implementation, example artifacts, signed package, Lean certificate, security and reproducibility materials, Windows and Ubuntu verification logs, review inputs, and an optional governed-AI provider demo. No API credentials are included. Test logs and provider results are project-owner evidence, not an independent security audit. The Windows and Ubuntu verification runs were recorded on 31 October 2026. Archive SHA-256: d347cb51591d7e1ee5e65a5903fe862663081574f027cdb9db86cf80a1a0027d. The archive and record are public for inspection and limited noncommercial evaluation under SharkLang Evaluation License 1.0, effective 1 November 2026. The license permits private evaluation, research, security review, testing, running the demo outside production, and private modification. Production or operational deployment, product or service integration, commercial use, redistribution of copies or modified versions, sublicensing, or providing the work as a service requires separate written permission; a commercial license may be available. publications.title: A robust calibration framework for t-z analysis of bored piles: Comparative assessment of hyperbolic and bilinear load-transfer models
publications.abstract: Although the t-z load-transfer method remains a cornerstone in geotechnical engineering, reliance on standardized empirical curves frequently introduces significant settlement prediction errors. To bridge this critical performance gap, this study develops an objective, automated back-analysis framework leveraging the generalized reduced gradient (GRG) nonlinear optimization algorithm (Excel Solver) to extract site-specific t-z and q-z parameters directly from full-scale static load tests. Integrating a one-dimensional finite difference model, the research evaluates the axial behavior of large-diameter bored piles by systematically comparing classical bilinear (elastic-perfectly plastic) and continuous nonlinear hyperbolic formulations against two rigorous benchmark datasets: Shibuya et al. (dense sand) and O’Neill et al. (cohesive clay). The results demonstrate that the hyperbolic model markedly out-performs the bilinear approach by gracefully capturing progressive soil stiffness degradation. Quantitatively, the hyperbolic formulation achieves exceptional predictive accuracy with Pearson correlation coefficients exceeding 0.997 and dramatically lower root mean square errors (RMSE) across both granular (1.234 MN for Shibuya) and cohesive (19.086 kN for O’Neill) strata, whereas the bilinear model exhibits severe error escalation (3.386 MN and 74.268 kN, respectively) despite maintaining relatively high correlation (R 2 ≈ 0.962 ÷ 0.975). Furthermore, comprehensive sensitivity analyses and Monte Carlo simulations (N=300) reveal that pile-head settlement is predominantly governed by initial stiffness mobilization rather than ultimate shear resistance, with sensitivity ratios reaching up to 30,000. By rigorously integrating automated optimization, statistical validation (t-tests), and probabilistic uncertainty quantification (95% confidence intervals), this study delivers a robust, efficient, and reliable methodology that significantly enhances the predictive confidence of modern pile foundation design.

publications.title: Operationalising Generative AI in Subsurface Operations: A Low-Code Well Passport Skill Built by the End User
publications.abstract: Abstract Subsurface teams in mature, high-well-count fields routinely spend 30 to 60 minutes per well gathering data before any technical evaluation can start. Across an inventory of more than 2,000 wells, that custodial work pulls scarce petrophysical and engineering time away from interpretation and decision-making. This paper describes the deployment and early field validation of a suite of AI-driven workflow automations on a mature onshore carbonate field. A domain petrophysicist authored them, not a central digital team, and they run on an enterprise generative-AI platform that the organisation had already deployed. The automations are grouped into five operational domains: (1) well intelligence, covering automated retrieval of formation tops, casing configuration, H₂S and CO₂ classification, saturation history and pressure records, together with on-request assembly of well documents; (2) cement integrity, covering automated bond-log interpretation across all casing strings with isolation-risk flagging; (3) petrophysical quick-look, covering real-time logging-while-drilling (LWD) processing from any service provider on the asset, with composite-log and interpretation-software-ready output; (4) logging-program generation for saturation and production programs, annotated with live-condition safety information; and (5) intervention reporting, which consolidates multi-contractor performance into a single management view. In field use, well-data retrieval time fell by more than 90 percent. Logging-program preparation dropped from one to three hours per well to under five minutes. Real-time petrophysical evaluation is now produced automatically at each drilling cycle to support landing decisions. Every output follows the corporate documentation standard, which removes the variation between engineers, and every value can be traced back to the source file it came from. The framework recovers an estimated four or more engineering hours per well event, needs no new infrastructure or software licences, and works with any logging service provider active on the field. It offers a practical and immediately replicable route to AI adoption for operations-intensive subsurface teams.

publications.title: A Multi-Agent Workflow for Structuring Development Planning Knowledge from Unstructured E&P Documents
publications.abstract: Abstract Development plans bring together multidisciplinary knowledge needed for reservoir evaluation, development deployment, and engineering decision-making. In practice, however, these documents are often lengthy, heterogeneous in format, and poorly standardized. This makes manual review slow and makes rule-based extraction prone to errors. To address this problem, this paper presents a multi-agent workflow for structuring knowledge from unstructured E&P documents, with private deployment and field application in an enterprise environment. The workflow is built on a customized orchestration engine. It integrates multimodal OCR parsing, long-context semantic understanding, complex table recognition, retrieval-augmented reasoning, and standardized output generation. Word, PDF, PNG, and other heterogeneous files are converted into structured Markdown and JSON formats, allowing semantic information to be extracted from text, tables, figures, merged cells, and embedded attachments. The proposed workflow consists of three task-oriented agents: a document parsing agent for layout recognition and content conversion, an indicator reasoning agent for identifying key indicators across long-document contexts, and a quality validation agent for multi-model cross-checking and rule-based quality control. The system has been deployed and validated in PetroChina's on-premise environment for development planning review. The validation covered more than 30 sets of documents and over 150 files, with the longest report exceeding 700 pages. Compared with manual review and rule-based extraction, the proposed method reduced the key indicator extraction cycle from approximately one week to eight minutes. After verification and quality control, the extraction accuracy reached 92%. The system generates eight categories of standardized outputs, covering geology and reservoir, engineering technology, economic evaluation, and other core planning results. These outputs support JSON export, data lake integration, reservoir modeling, inter-well dynamic analysis, and comparison of historical development plans.

publications.title: Guara: Make AI Knowledge Verifiable
publications.abstract: Guara 0.1.3 Guara 0.1.3 brings the new maned wolf identity, clearer onboarding, reliable connection cleanup, and a tested, complete installation bundle. Python distribution and CLI names remain opentruth. Changes A documentation index and Brazilian Portuguese getting-started guide. Clearer runtime/development installation, Windows activation, and workspace selection. Consolidated current backup, integrity, pagination, and reassessment guidance. Guará, a Brazilian maned wolf mascot, with usage and accessibility guidance. DOI citation metadata: 10.5281/zenodo.23870405. opentruth --version reports the installed distribution version without opening a store. with OpenTruth(workspace) as app: closes the SQLite connection on success and exceptions. Local Markdown/image-link validation and installed-wheel CLI validation. UTF-8 stdout/stderr on all platforms, including Windows redirected scientific text. Complete CLI convenience flags for search filters, evidence links, claim/evidence revisions, reviews, attribution, and comparison tolerances. End-to-end CLI lifecycle and failed-mutation atomicity tests, including restored audit history. Automated complete ZIP and SHA-256 manifest generation from validated wheel/source inputs. Packaging regressions reject mismatched versions, duplicate files, traversal, symlinks, and nested old deliveries. English LinkedIn artwork with a prominent repository link, including white-background and cartoon-scientist variants. Compatibility No schema change: schema 2, evidence statuses, JSON CLI defaults, and the twelve MCP tools are preserved. Python 3.11+ is required. Runtime remains offline after dependency installation. Secure local source ingestion remains POSIX-only; Windows supports metadata workflows. Back up existing evidence before upgrading. Install the supplied wheel with python -m pip install /path/to/opentruth-0.1.3-py3-none-any.whl, then run opentruth --version. See the installation guide. The product and remote repository are named Guara. The owner completed the remote rename, confirmed through GitHub API. See compatibility details. See the local validation results for the checks executed on this deliverable. Downloads Use Guara-0.1.3.zip for the complete product, or install opentruth-0.1.3-py3-none-any.whl in a Python 3.11+ virtual environment. SHA256SUMS covers each downloadable artifact. The ZIP contains a Guara/ directory; open COMECE-AQUI.md after extraction. CI gates publication on Linux, macOS, and Windows with Python 3.11–3.13. PyPI publication is a separate, optional maintainer workflow and is not part of this release.
